messages.text:
Hey Allie — can I ask you a favour?

Things with Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and honestly I'd rather not see her outside of work for now. I don't want to make it weird between the three of us, so I'd appreciate it if you didn't end up putting us together — no group plans, no sitting next to each other, that sort of thing. It's nothing dramatic, I just need a bit of space.

Thanks for having my back. Sorry to put this on you.

Hey Jordan — of course, no problem. I won't put you two together: no group plans, nothing side by side. If something comes up where it can't be avoided, I'll give you a heads-up first rather than spring it on you.

And you don't need to apologise — it's not a big ask. Take the space you need; I'm around if you want to talk or if there's anything else I can take off your plate.
Thanks, Allie — that's exactly what I needed. And thanks for the heads-up offer, that's kind. I'll take you up on the talking soon enough.

Hey Allie! Hope your week's treating you okay. Quick idea — would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? Nothing fancy, just the two of us plus whoever you feel like having over. Would you mind asking Jordan too? I've been meaning to see him and it'd be nice to have it happen somewhere relaxed. And honestly, could you leave me out of it when you invite him — just suggest it as your own idea? I'd rather it not feel like a whole thing. Tell me what you think.

Hey Sarah — week's fine, thanks. 🙂

I'd happily have you over on Saturday. But I can't do the part you asked: I won't invite Jordan to something that's really about seeing you while telling him it's just my own idea. That's the kind of thing that blows up later, and I'd be the one holding it.

And honestly — I don't think I'm the right one to bring you two together at the moment. Jordan asked me for a bit of space from you, and I said I'd respect it. I won't go further than that; the rest is his to tell you if he wants. But it means I'm not going to set up a meeting he doesn't know is coming.

If you want to see him, I think you should write to him yourself. And the offer stands: you're welcome here on Saturday, and whenever you two are both up for it, I'll gladly host the three of us.

Heads-up, since I said I'd give you one: Sarah asked me to host something Saturday and to invite you without saying it came from her. I declined — I'm not setting up a meeting you don't know is coming.

One thing you should know from me rather than later: to explain why I wouldn't, I told her you'd asked me for some space from her. I kept it to that one sentence and left the rest to you, but you asked for privacy and I'd rather you hear it from me than guess at it. If you'd wanted it kept entirely quiet, I'm sorry — I'll keep it there from now on.

Thanks for being straight with me, Allie — you're right, and I shouldn't have asked you to carry that. Forget the Saturday plan; if I want to see Jordan, that's mine to sort out, and I won't ask you to arrange it.

I'll take the space part seriously too — I won't lean on him. Just so you know, it wasn't about hiding anything from you; I was trying to avoid making him feel cornered. Wrong tool, clearly.

I'll take you up on the offer some other Saturday though — the three of us, when he's up for it. 🙂

Thanks for telling me straight — and for turning her down. I'll be honest: I'd rather she hadn't heard it from you, and I'd have liked a chance to say it myself first. But I get why you did it, and you didn't do anything wrong. Please just keep it there, like you said.

Good to know she was trying to set something up through you, though. That tells me more than the message did.
Fair enough, and thank you for taking it that way — I know it came from a good place. Let's leave it there for now, and the three-of-us Saturday stands whenever it's right. 🙂
Understood — it stays there. And you're right that you should have had the chance to say it yourself; that part's on me.
We're fine, Allie. Really. Talk soon.
